Vital signs are normal and there is no fever, GI, or respiratory symptoms, making systemic infection or GI emergency less likely. Normal CBC and a foot X‑ray without fracture reduce likelihood of osteomyelitis or bony injury. Crucially, exam revealed a reddened, swollen left second toe with a constricting hair/thread identified — this local finding directly explains focal pain and irritability. A hair-thread (hair tourniquet) can rapidly constrict soft tissue, causing ischemia and significant pain in infants who cannot localize discomfort. The combination of a focal swollen erythematous toe with an identified constricting hair and otherwise unremarkable systemic evaluation makes hair-tourniquet syndrome the most likely diagnosis and a clinical emergency requiring prompt removal to restore circulation and prevent tissue necrosis.

DIAGNOSIS: Hair (hair-thread) tourniquet of the left second toe (hair-tourniquet syndrome)
